prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1073; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of rear-end collision at intersection. Insured vehicle stopped at light, struck from behind by third-party vehicle. Claimant reports neck strain and stiffness, seeking medical evaluation. No attorney on file; claimant handling communications directly.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Confirmed injury is neck strain, with pain radiating to shoulder and limited rotation. Claimant has seen urgent care and received a prescription for muscle relaxants. Provided information on the bodily injury claim process and requested medical records and itemized bills. Claimant stated they have not retained counsel.

Entry 3: Received photos of both vehicles from claimant showing rear bumper damage to the third-party vehicle and minor trunk damage to the claimant's vehicle. Police report obtained and reviewed; it notes the at-fault driver admitted following too closely. Liability appears clear. Advised claimant that they may consult an attorney at any time if they wish.

Entry 4: Requested authorization for release of medical records from claimant. Claimant signed and returned the form. Records from urgent care reviewed; diagnosis consistent with cervical strain, no fractures or imaging-confirmed injuries noted. Follow-up with primary care physician scheduled per claimant report.

Entry 5: Claimant contacted office to ask about rental car coverage and status of physical therapy referral. Explained rental reimbursement terms and that the bodily injury evaluation remains open pending treatment updates. Set reminder to request physical therapy progress notes in thirty days. Claim remains active, no settlement offered at this time.
